excerpt: Houston Texans won 34-31. The spread pushed and the reasoning did not hold.
seo_description: Houston Texans beat Jacksonville Jaguars 34-31. EdgeDesk’s number implied Jacksonville Jaguars +3 — push. 0 of 9 gradeable claims held up, 7 did not. Process grade: UNSOUND. Research, not picks.
model_status_note: The spread pushed and the reasoning did not hold.

implied_side.why: EdgeDesk’s own number sat 5.2 points toward Jacksonville Jaguars of the quote EdgeDesk captured at BetRivers. That is what the disagreement implied. It was published as research, not as a recommendation to bet it.

implied_total.why: EdgeDesk’s fair total of 41.5 sat 1.5 points below the captured total of 43.

closing_line.note: The line moved 5.5 points toward the side EdgeDesk’s number leaned before kickoff. That is the market arriving where EdgeDesk already was, and over many games it is the only evidence that a disagreement carried information.

reasons: 6 of 8 gradeable claims went the other way. The read of this matchup was wrong in its mechanism, not only in its number.
The result carries 1 high-variance marker — the spread result changed on the final score — so the scoreboard is weaker evidence than it looks.
EdgeDesk projected a home margin of 2.2 and the game finished 3 the away way — 5.2 points of margin error, inside the range the model published.
process.basis: the drivers, matchups and measured advantages only — never the price or the market claim, which are the result in longer words

variance_markers.label: The spread result changed on the final score
variance_markers.text: Before the last scoring play of the game the spread graded win; it finished push. A number that moves on a score taken in the last minutes of a decided game is a scoreboard event, not a matchup one.

variance_markers.label: A 3-point game
variance_markers.text: A game this close is decided inside the noise of any projection. Whichever way it fell, it is weak evidence about either team.

verdict.line: The spread pushed and the reasoning did not hold.

grading.separation_note: The bet result and the process grade above are computed separately and are allowed to disagree. A winning number with a broken thesis is recorded as exactly that.

lessons.pregame_expectation: 4 of the claims in this article rested on market, model, pressure.
lessons.actual_result: None of them could be graded: the result landed exactly on the market number — a push settles nothing about the disagreement; no single-game statistic in EdgeDesk’s vocabulary observes this driver.
lessons.lesson: EdgeDesk prices these games partly on signals it has no way to observe afterwards. That is not an error in the model — it is a gap in the audit, and it means the platform cannot tell, from results alone, whether those parts of the number are earning their weight.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Consider whether a postgame data source exists for market, model, pressure.

lessons.lesson: A total missed by this much usually means a pace or a finishing assumption was wrong, not that both ratings were. Check which of the two moved.
lessons.suggested_investigation: Was the play count or the points per drive the miss? Both are in this game’s result record.
